parts:
Hi,

PARDISO support for Windows is a little experimental.

the newest testing version has and 'experimental' build,

$ ls ~/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.6/INLA/bin/windows/
32bit/  64bit/  experimental/


and by controlling 'inla.call', like in Linux

> inla.getOption('inla.call')
[1] "/home/hrue/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.6/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl.run"


you can set 'inla.call' to either 'inla.exe' or 'inla-mkl.exe' in that experimental directory

inla.setOption(inla.call='...../experimental/inla-mkl.exe')


there was some issues still with slow speed on some operations, but might be worth trying.

after setting the license file, you can do

> inla.pardiso.check()
[1] "SUCCESS: PARDISO IS INSTALLED AND WORKING"


and you should hopefully get this...

H



On Thu, 2019-12-05 at 09:26 -0800, TDM wrote:
Hi all,

As recently reported by others, I am no longer able to use INLA for large data sets. Below is some code for reproducing the problem (data attached to this message).

If you run the code, you'll see that a simple model crashes with 100K records but runs with 30K records. I tried a bunch of control.inla and control.compute options, just in case defaults have changed in recent test versions of INLA, but I haven't got it to work. Then I thought I needed to get the Pardiso libraries under the assumption that these were now required for larger data sets. Unfortunately, I am not a computer whiz, and I haven't been able to get Pardiso to work. I downloaded the three Pardiso files for Windows, put them in their own directory (C:/Pardiso) and pointed INLA to the licence, but I get errors (FAILURE: PARDISO IS NOT INSTALLED OR NOT WORKING). I am sure there is more to configuring Pardiso, but have no clue what to do. So, my questions:

(1) Am I doing something wrong in the example code?
(2) If not, can anyone provide detailed configuration for the latest version of Pardiso (6.2) for a Windows machine?
(3) If not, can I somehow download an older version of INLA that still works with large data sets?

Thanks a ton!
Tim

# set up
library(dplyr)
library(INLA)
setwd("C:/Users/tmeehan/Downloads/")

# get data
dat1 <- read.csv("eg_data.csv")
summary(dat1)

# make formula
form1 <- count ~ year

# run model on all data
lm1 <- lm(form1, data=dat1)
inla1 <- inla(form1, data=dat1, verbose=T,
              control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="eb"),
              control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="default", smtp="default"))
summary(lm1)
summary(inla1)

# thin data
dat2 <- dat1 %>% sample_n(size=30000)

# run model on less data
lm2 <- lm(form1, data=dat2)
inla2 <- inla(form1, data=dat2, verbose=T,
              control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="eb"),
              control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="default", smtp="default"))
summary(lm2)
summary(inla2)

# need pardiso?
inla.setOption(pardiso.license="C:/Users/tmeehan/pardiso.lic")
inla.pardiso.check()
inla.pardiso()

--

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA Now Crashes With Large Data Sets
parts:
There hasn't been any changes in the main body of the code which
should indicate that it crash, ie runs out of memory, earlier than
before.

There are strategies to reduce the ammount of memory used

- reduce the number of threads used, like

inla(..., num.threads=2)

- remove the integration step, like

inla(..., control.inla=list(int.strategy='eb'))

- use an adaptive strategy, like

inla(..., control.inla=list(strategy='adaptive'))


- run on MacOSX or Linux. Windows seems to have 'issues' with larger
models, I do not use Win so do not know if there is something to be
done from the OS side.

H

I have had problems like this in the past, although I’ve noticed that when I do something that feels like it should be analogous: running (aggregated) count models with trials / offsets indicating hundreds of thousands of trials / exposures, albeit only in 40k or so levels of said “observations,” INLA handles it swiftly and with aplomb in Windows as well as Linux, particularly when I enable MKL in INLA for Windows.  I do tend to switch to an exclusive gaussian strategy when I do this, as the data set is large enough that the additional corrections do not seem to matter much for some of these models.  But we may have to keep iterating to better understand where some of these errors come from.  Sorry I cannot be of more help.

 

Jonathan

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA Now Crashes With Large Data Sets
parts:
I just set up an Ubuntu VM on my Windows machine, loaded the latest R and R-INLA, and everything works fine. So either I messed up my Windows R configuration somehow, or a Windows update messed it up for me. Anyway, if anyone else has this problem, this is one workaround.

# test

# set up
library(dplyr)
library(INLA)

# make data
n <- 100000
x=ceiling(runif(n, 0, 12))
y=ceiling(100 + 2*x + rnorm(n, x, 10))
dat1 <- data.frame(y, x)
plot(y~x, data=dat1)
head(dat1)
summary(dat1)

# make formula
form1 <- y ~ x

# run model on all data
lm1 <- lm(form1, data=dat1)
inla1 <- inla(form1, data=dat1, verbose=T,
              control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="eb"),
              control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="default", smtp="default"))
summary(lm1)
summary(inla1)

# thin data
dat2 <- dat1 %>% sample_n(size=30000)

# run model on less data
lm2 <- lm(form1, data=dat2)
inla2 <- inla(form1, data=dat2, verbose=T,
              control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="eb"),
              control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="default", smtp="default"))
summary(lm2)
summary(inla2)

# need pardiso?
inla.setOption(pardiso.license="C:/Users/tmeehan/pardiso.lic")
inla.pardiso.check()
# inla.pardiso()

maybe this is a good 'workaround'? then it seems it that there is
'something' in the Windows system that does not allow a process to
take to much of the resources? or that there is an option that is set
so; I don't know, as I do not use Windows.

I know in Linux, there is 'ulimit' to control some of this within the
shell, like

$ ulimit -a
core file size (blocks, -c) unlimited
data seg size (kbytes, -d) unlimited
scheduling priority (-e) 0
file size (blocks, -f) unlimited
pending signals (-i) 63268
max locked memory (kbytes, -l) 64
max memory size (kbytes, -m) unlimited
open files (-n) 1024
pipe size (512 bytes, -p) 8
POSIX message queues (bytes, -q) 819200
real-time priority (-r) 0
stack size (kbytes, -s) unlimited
cpu time (seconds, -t) unlimited
max user processes (-u) 63268
virtual memory (kbytes, -v) unlimited
file locks (-x) unlimited



at some point, ie looong time ago that I recall, there was a similar
issue, and the solution was to go maximum. so I still have

ulimit $(for opt in c d s t f n; do echo -n "-$opt unlimited ";done)
>/dev/null 2>&1


in my ~/.bashrc, but I don't know if I really need it anymore...

H
